Hi Ethan — appreciate the details. Attached is the proposal I mentioned (redwood-proposal-v2.pdf) and the small usage workbook we populated with your 3.5M peak and stated budget bands (finity-usage-models.xlsx). Below is the worked example you asked for — numbers are illustrative and assume current quantized model profile with conservative cache hit rates.

Worked examples (blended, $/1M tokens):
- Scenario A: Pilot / validation (60M tokens/month) — blended $/1M = $1,850
  - Assumptions: 70% route A at model-v1 (higher quality), 30% route B at model-lite (quantized), peak buffering covered by burst credits

- Scenario B: Mid-commit (120M tokens/month) — blended $/1M = $1,320
  - Assumptions: same mix; we apply 12% volume discount + routing optimization (higher cache reuse on summaries)

- Scenario C: Step-up (240M tokens/month) — blended $/1M = $960
  - Assumptions: larger reserved capacity (Dedicated pool), higher batching, and optional model-shelfing for bulk batch jobs

Breakpoints to watch:
- Crossing 100M tokens/month typically unlocks better route-level discounts (we can reconfigure routing to favor model-lite for low-latency audit runs)
- Any route that is >40% of total tokens should be considered for a dedicated optimization lane (saves ~8–12% on unit cost)

Attachments included:
- redwood-proposal-v2.pdf — line-item pricing, SLA notes, and commitment-term options
- finity-usage-models.xlsx — editable workbook with token mixes and sensitivity tabs

Proposed commercial path:
1) Pilot (4 weeks) — capped at $60k for first month, scope as discussed.
2) If pilot meets quality bar, convert to 6mo committed volume with monthly billing and a step-up clause at month 3 to reevaluate and potentially shift to 12mo pricing.

Action items:
- Ethan: confirm procurement contacts so legal can send the SOW/PO template (Priya, please advise)
- Priya: verify that the pilot cap and the peak 3.5M/day are acceptable to stakeholders
- Marissa / Aditya: I’ve cc’d you to help with any technical clarifications and to own the pricing cadence if we move to committed volume

Thanks — I’ll stand by for procurement contacts and your pilot confirmation.

Best,
